claim: Pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) can be found in numerous cell types, particularly in the postsynaptic membrane of the vertebrate nervous system, where they transduce electrochemical signals upon neurotransmitter binding.
source: Pentameric ligand-gated ion channels (pLGICs) can be found in numerous cell types, particularly in the postsynaptic membrane of the vertebrate nervous system, where they transduce electrochemical signals upon neurotransmitter binding (Tasneem et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tasneem et al., 2005

claim: Gating in pLGICs is initiated by ligand binding in the extracellular domain (ECD), which is believed to lead to large twisting and blooming motions in the ECD, followed by rearrangements in the transmembrane domain (TMD), which eventually lead to opening of the central transmembrane pore.
source: Gating in pLGICs is initiated by ligand binding in the extracellular domain (ECD), which is believed to lead to large twisting and blooming motions in the ECD, followed by rearrangements in the transmembrane domain (TMD), which eventually lead to opening of the central transmembrane pore.
evidence: Draws from established understanding of pLGIC gating mechanisms

claim: Lipid components of the plasma membrane have been shown to bind to a variety of membrane proteins, potentially modifying their stability or gating.
source: In addition to soluble ligands and numerous allosteric modulators, lipid components of the plasma membrane have been shown to bind to a variety of membrane proteins, potentially modifying their stability or gating (Duncan et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Duncan et al., 2020

claim: Lipid composition was shown to influence reconstitution of functional activity in the Torpedo nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) as early as the 1980s.
source: For pLGICs, lipid composition was shown to influence reconstitution of functional activity in the Torpedo nicotinic acetylcholine receptor (nAChR) as early as the 1980s (Popot et al., 1981; Criado et al., 1982; Fong and McNamee, 1986; daCosta et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations from the 1980s and 2002

claim: Multiple members of the pLGIC family, particularly nAChRs and prokaryotic channels cloned from Gloeobacter violaceus (GLIC) and Dickeya dadantii (formerly Erwinia chrysanthemi, reflected in the channel name ELIC), have demonstrated functional sensitivity or co-purification with membrane lipids.
source: Multiple members of the pLGIC family, particularly nAChRs and prokaryotic channels cloned from Gloeobacter violaceus (GLIC) and Dickeya dadantii (formerly Erwinia chrysanthemi, reflected in the channel name ELIC), have since demonstrated functional sensitivity or co-purification with membrane lipids (Thompson and Baenziger, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Thompson and Baenziger, 2020

claim: It has been suggested that lipids interact with membrane-facing loops from the ECD, or with the four membrane-spanning helices (M1-M4) of the TMD.
source: It has been suggested that lipids interact with membrane-facing loops from the ECD, or with the four membrane-spanning helices (M1-M4) of the TMD.
evidence: Represents a hypothesis or suggestion from the literature

claim: Many structural details of lipid interactions with pLGICs remain poorly understood.
source: However, many structural details of these lipid interactions remain poorly understood (Poveda et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Poveda et al., 2017

claim: A critical challenge to elucidating lipid-protein interactions is their typically poor definition in experimental densities.
source: A critical challenge to elucidating lipid-protein interactions is their typically poor definition in experimental densities.
evidence: Represents a known limitation in structural biology

claim: Among more than 100 deposited structures in the protein data bank for GLIC crystallized under activating conditions, several lipid poses have been reported.
source: Among more than 100 deposited structures in the protein data bank for GLIC crystallized under activating conditions, several lipid poses have been reported (Zhu et al., 2018; Masiulis et al., 2019; Laverty et al., 2019; Walsh et al., 2018; Gharpure et al., 2019; Rahman et al., 2020; Zhao et al., 2021).

claim: Reported lipid poses in GLIC structures include an outer-leaflet site on the complementary face of a single GLIC subunit, an inner-leaflet site on the principal face of a subunit, and an interfacial inner-leaflet site making contacts with two neighboring subunits.
source: These include an outer-leaflet site on the complementary face of a single GLIC subunit, an inner-leaflet site on the principal face of a subunit, and an interfacial inner-leaflet site making contacts with two neighboring subunits (Thompson and Baenziger, 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Thompson and Baenziger, 2020

claim: In one case, an additional outer-leaflet density was built as a detergent molecule.

claim: The positions and orientations of membrane components or mimetics vary between structures and typically include only a subset of their constituent atoms.
source: However, the positions and orientations of these membrane components or mimetics vary between structures and typically include only a subset of their constituent atoms.

claim: No lipids were reported with the lone X-ray structure of GLIC under resting conditions.
source: No lipids were reported with the lone X-ray structure of GLIC under resting conditions, raising the possibility that interactions could be state-dependent, or obscured by the relatively low overall resolution of this dataset (4.0 Å) (Sauguet et al., 2014).

claim: The absence of lipids in the resting-state GLIC structure raises the possibility that interactions could be state-dependent, or obscured by the relatively low overall resolution of this dataset (4.0 Å).

source: All-atom simulations of membrane proteins typically involve inserting an experimental structure in a simplified lipid bilayer surrounded by water and ions, all of which move freely according to physical principles encoded in the force field.

source: Simulations on both atomistic and coarse-grained levels have recently enabled the identification of specific lipid interactions in pLGICs such as ELIC (Sridhar et al., 2021; Dietzen et al., 2022), nAChRs (Sharp and Brannigan, 2021), glycine (Dämgen and Biggin, 2021), and serotonin-3 receptors (Crnjar and Molteni, 2021), but were typically limited to shorter timescales or specific protein conformations.

claim: Previous simulations of pLGICs were typically limited to shorter timescales or specific protein conformations.

source: Because GLIC is activated by external acidification (pH < 6), resting versus activating conditions could be approximated throughout these simulations by setting titratable amino acid residues as deprotonated versus protonated, respectively.

source: Lipids built in this structure formed close contacts with GLIC residues in several membrane-proximal regions. These included an ECD motif with a characteristic proline/cysteine-rich turn, known as the Pro-loop (or Cys-loop in eukaryotes); N-terminal residues of the M1 helix; regions in and surrounding the M2-M3 loop; interfacial residues at the C-terminal end of M3; and inward- and outward-facing regions of M4 (Figure 2A).

evidence: Represents a claim of novelty based on literature review and current findings

claim: The GLIC sample was solubilized in detergent, which is typically thought to replace biological lipids.
source: Notably, the GLIC sample was solubilized in detergent, which is typically thought to replace biological lipids.

claim: MD simulations have recently been used to identify lipid binding sites corresponding to experimental data for both prokaryotic and eukaryotic ligand-gated ion channels.

claim: The slow rate of lateral lipid diffusion has resulted in the preferential use of coarse-grained force fields able to sample longer timescales, but that may overestimate the strength of interactions.

claim: Previous simulation studies typically apply harmonic restraints to the protein, potentially obscuring contributions of protein dynamics to lipid interactions.
source: In addition, such studies typically apply harmonic restraints to the protein, potentially obscuring contributions of protein dynamics to lipid interactions.
evidence: Represents a limitation of previous simulation approaches

claim: The unrestrained atomistic MD simulations studied here were not expected to capture the maximal duration of stable contacts, as indicated by some interaction times approaching the full 1.7 µs trajectory.
source: Indeed, the unrestrained atomistic MD simulations studied here were not expected to capture the maximal duration of stable contacts, as indicated by some interaction times approaching the full 1.7 µs trajectory (Figure 2).
evidence: Represents an acknowledgment of simulation limitations, supported by figure reference

claim: Simulations were of sufficient length to sample exchange of up to four lipids, particularly around the M4 helix.
source: Nevertheless, simulations were of sufficient length to sample exchange of up to four lipids, particularly around the M4 helix.
evidence: Represents findings from the simulation data

claim: Calculation of lipid lateral diffusion coefficients resulted in average displacements at the end of simulations of 2.15 nm for lipids initially interacting with the protein surface, roughly corresponding to lipids diffusing out to the fourth lipid shell.
source: Calculation of lipid lateral diffusion coefficients resulted in average displacements at the end of simulations of 2.15 nm for lipids initially interacting with the protein surface, roughly corresponding to lipids diffusing out to the fourth lipid shell.

claim: Diffusion of bulk lipids was faster, allowing lipids originally 3.16 nm away from the protein surface to ingress the first lipid shell.

claim: Diffusion metrics underscore the potential for lipid exchange events even among lipids initially distant from the protein surface.
source: This observation underscores the potential for lipid exchange events even among lipids initially distant from the protein surface.

claim: Prior experiments have been conducted to assess the sensitivity of GLIC in varying lipid environments, indicating that GLIC remains fully functional in pure POPC bilayers.
source: Prior experiments have been conducted to assess the sensitivity of GLIC in varying lipid environments (Labriola et al., 2013; Carswell et al., 2015; Menny et al., 2017), indicating that GLIC remains fully functional in pure POPC bilayers.

claim: In the cryo-EM experiments, the protein was recombinantly expressed from Escherichia coli, which means that the experimental density would likely represent phosphatidylglycerol or phosphatidylethanolamine lipids.

source: However, as the molecular identities of bound lipids could not be precisely determined, POPC lipids were built for straightforward comparison with simulation poses.

claim: It remains plausible that GLIC function could be influenced by different lipid species, especially due to the presence of multiple charged residues around the TMD/ECD interface which might interact differently with different lipid head groups.
source: While it appears that GLIC is capable of gating in a pure POPC bilayer, it remains plausible that its function could be influenced by different lipid species, especially due to the presence of multiple charged residues around the TMD/ECD interface which might interact differently with different lipid head groups.
evidence: Represents speculation about potential lipid-specific effects

claim: The authors were able to identify both long-lasting and highly occupied lipid sites by analyzing a large number of parallel trajectories (500 instances of each subunit).
source: In simulations, we were able to identify both long-lasting and highly occupied lipid sites by analyzing a large number of parallel trajectories (500 instances of each subunit).

claim: Simulation frames could be classified into closed or open states by projection onto a previously published Markov state model of GLIC gating, which had been validated against electrophysiology recordings and structural features.
source: Simulation frames could further be classified into closed or open states by projection onto a previously published Markov state model of GLIC gating, which had been validated against electrophysiology recordings and structural features (Bergh et al., 2021).
evidence: Describes the analysis method, supported by citation to previous work

claim: As simulations were initiated by placing the GLIC structures in generated POPC bilayers, it is reassuring that lipid binding sites identified in simulations appear to correspond closely to densities representing lipids bound tightly enough in the cryo-EM data to be retained during reconstitution.
source: In particular, as simulations were initiated by placing the GLIC structures in generated POPC bilayers, it is reassuring that lipid binding sites identified in simulations appear to correspond closely to densities representing lipids bound tightly enough in the cryo-EM data to be retained during reconstitution (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D).
evidence: Represents validation of the simulation approach by comparison with cryo-EM data

claim: The occupational densities varied remarkably little between resting and activating conditions, indicating state rather than pH dependence in lipid interactions.
source: Interestingly, the occupational densities varied remarkably little between resting and activating conditions (Figure 1—figure supplement 1), indicating state rather than pH dependence in lipid interactions, also further justifying the approach of merging closed-state GLIC cryo-EM datasets collected at different pH conditions to resolve lipids.
evidence: Represents an interpretation of the simulation data, supported by figure reference

claim: The three lipids identified in the inner leaflet may play primarily structural roles, as they did not vary substantially between closed and open states.
source: The three lipids identified in the inner leaflet may play primarily structural roles, as they did not vary substantially between closed and open states (Figure 5).
evidence: Represents speculation based on the lack of state dependence, supported by figure reference

claim: Principal-face and intersubunit sites in the closed cryo-EM structure were largely superimposable with those in open X-ray structures.

evidence: Represents a comparison between current and previous structural data, supported by figure references

claim: A lipid in the intersubunit site was also reported in previous open-state X-ray structures of GLIC.

claim: The W217A substitution was previously shown to suppress GLIC function and was considered the most impactful of several aromatic residues on the transmembrane surface.

claim: A lack of double bonds in the intercalating tail was associated with the lipid head group interacting more closely with the protein surface, indicating a possible role for saturation in overall lipid-binding modes.

claim: At the complementary-face site, simulations indicated that lipid tails could penetrate deeper into the helical bundle upon channel opening, and even further in a state associated with desensitization.
source: At the complementary-face site - one of the most consistently documented in previous X-ray structures - simulations indicated that lipid tails could penetrate deeper into the helical bundle upon channel opening (Figure 5B), and even further in a state associated with desensitization (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).

claim: Buried portions of the complementary-face site have been shown to host allosteric modulators such as propofol, substituting for lipid-tail interactions.

source: State dependence was also suggested at the principal-face site, where the lipid head preferred a pose tilted in toward M3 in the closed state, but tilted out toward M4 in the open state.

claim: The closed cryo-EM structure was more consistent with open-state simulations, and with a detergent built in an open X-ray structure.
source: However, our closed cryo-EM structure was more consistent with open-state simulations, and with a detergent built in an open X-ray structure (Hu et al., 2018).

source: Although lipids have yet to be resolved at this intersubunit site in GLIC, they have been reported in open-state structures of both ELIC (Petroff et al., 2022) and GluCl (Althoff et al., 2014), and in a desensitized neuronal GABA(A) receptor (Laverty et al., 2019).

claim: This work demonstrates the combined power of cryo-EM and MD simulations to characterize membrane-protein lipid interactions.
source: Finally, this work demonstrates the combined power of cryo-EM and MD simulations to characterize membrane-protein lipid interactions.

claim: In leveraging extensive MD simulations to build lipids for the first time into a closed-state structure of GLIC, the authors were able to capture features of lipid-tail saturation and potential state dependence that were not available from structural data alone.
